CT CORONARY ANGIOGRAPHY

Clinical details: 42-year-old woman. Intermittent left-sided chest tightness, not related to exertion. QRISK3 6%. ?Coronary artery disease.

Technique:
Non-contrast prospectively gated calcium score acquisition followed by prospectively ECG-triggered CT coronary angiography.
Heart rate 57 bpm, sinus rhythm. Metoprolol 5 mg IV. GTN 800 micrograms sublingual.
Contrast: Omnipaque 350, 60 ml.
DLP 142 mGy.cm (estimated effective dose 3.7 mSv).

Calcium score:
Total Agatston score 0.

Coronary arteries:
Right dominant.
Normal coronary origins and course.
LMS: no plaque.
LAD: no plaque. Diagonals unremarkable.
LCx: no plaque. Obtuse marginals unremarkable.
RCA: no plaque.
No myocardial bridging.

Non-coronary findings:
Cardiac chambers normal in size. No pericardial effusion.
The left atrial appendage is well opacified with no filling defect to suggest thrombus.
Ascending aorta 31 mm. Pulmonary trunk 24 mm.
Visualised lung bases unremarkable. No significant extracardiac findings.

Conclusion:
1. No coronary artery calcium and no coronary plaque. CAD-RADS 0.
2. No significant non-coronary findings.
